title: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital
byline: A fire has broken out in the children’s ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad, killing at least 15 newborns, according to local media.

title: Man died of extreme cold in plane landing gear
byline: An unidentified man found in a plane’s wheel compartment at Gatwick Airport died after being exposed to extreme cold and a lack of oxygen, an inquest has heard.

title: Police tighten security in Kandy ahead of fourth Randoli Perahera
byline: Security measures have been intensified across Kandy as police prepare for the fourth Randoli Perahera of the annual Kandy Esala Maha Perahera Festival today (26).

title: Joint emergency response mechanism established at Jaffna Prison
byline: A joint coordination mechanism involving state agencies has been established at Jaffna Prison to strengthen regional responses to emergencies and improve coordination during incidents within the prison system.

title: Probe underway into viral video from Ambalangoda Police Station
byline: Police have launched an investigation into a video circulating on social media showing an incident that allegedly took place inside the Ambalangoda Police Station. The inquiry was ordered by Inspector General of Police (IGP).

title: Drought preparedness must begin before crisis, Sri Lanka tells UNCCD COP17
byline: Sri Lanka has highlighted the need to strengthen drought preparedness and resilience before drought conditions develop into a crisis, calling for increased international support for developing countries.

title: Iran and Oman discuss temporary Hormuz corridor as impasse with US drags on
byline: Iran said it had restarted talks ​with neighbor Oman to manage the Strait of Hormuz as it faces heightened economic pressure from U.S. ‌President Donald Trump in the wider conflict.

title: Dolly Parton, country music icon and ‘Jolene’ singer, dies at 80
byline: Dolly Parton, who rose from humble beginnings to the greatest heights of American music and became one of the country’s most philanthropic, unifying and beloved stars, died Tuesday in Nashville, according to a family statement. She was 80.

title: Bus driver jailed for 13 years for high-speed crash that killed seven
byline: The Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal filed by a private bus driver and affirmed his conviction and 13-year-and-three-month rigorous imprisonment sentence for causing the deaths of seven people and injuries to dozens of others in a fatal road accident near Chilaw in 2017.

title: El Nino: Health Sector bracing for weather related diseases
byline: With the El Niño weather phenomena set to trigger rainfall higher than normal, to be followed by a dry spell, the Health Ministry is gearing up to deal with a possible rise in climate-related diseases, an official said yesterday.

title: Government hospitals still face Filgrastim shortage
byline: Health Minister Nalinda Jayatissa yesterday acknowledged that the shortage of the cancer drug Filgrastim continues in government hospitals, but said the supplier had assured that a consignment would be airlifted within a week.

title: 47 tortoises rescued from drought-hit pond in Kantale
byline: Wildlife officers have rescued 47 tortoises after they became trapped in a pond that had dried up amid severe drought conditions in the Kantale area.

title: Prophet Muhammad’s teachings offer strength to fight drugs and build a just society: President
byline: Claiming that Islam rejects all forms of vice that corrupt both the inner purity of the individual and the moral fabric of society, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said the teachings and example of the Holy Prophet Muhammad provide immense strength to programmes aimed at uplifting the moral fabric of society, such as the national campaign launched by the Government to combat the scourge of illicit drugs,

title: Manjrekar slams ICC, BCCI after Jaiswal gets only demerit point for confrontation with Fernando
byline: Former India cricketer Sanjay Manjrekar has expressed his disappointment with the International Cricket Council (ICC) and Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) after Indian opener Yashasvi Jaiswal was handed only a lenient punishment for his aggressive confrontation with Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando.

title: 13 motorcycles handed over to wildlife officers in Trincomalee
byline: Thirteen motorcycles have been handed over to field officers of the Department of Wildlife Conservation in the Trincomalee District to strengthen wildlife protection efforts, curb forest-related offences and improve the response to the growing human-elephant conflict.

title: Sri Lanka’s economy nears pre-crisis level: CBSL Chief
byline: The national economy has recovered to almost its pre-crisis level following a sharp turnaround from its worst economic meltdown, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said this week, pointing to stronger public finances, improved fiscal balances and progress towards debt sustainability as key pillars of the recovery.

title: Eleven new envoys present credentials to President
byline: Eleven newly appointed Ambassadors and High Commissioners to Sri Lanka presented their credentials to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat yesterday (25).

title: Namal calls for immediate action against online abuse networks
byline: SLPP National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has called on the Government to take immediate action over reports of WhatsApp, Facebook and Telegram networks allegedly being used to distribute intimate images without consent and exploit women, children and other vulnerable individuals.

title: Guidance of Holy Prophet Muhammad as an exemplar of peace vital for  coexistence in a multi-ethnic society: Sajith
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa said today that the guidance of Holy Prophet Muhammed is important for coexistence in a multi-ethnic society.

title: Heavy traffic reported at several expressway entrances and exits
byline: Heavy traffic congestion has been reported at several entrances and exits of Sri Lanka’s expressway network as motorists travel during the long weekend holiday that began today.

title: Nuwara Eliya records lowest minimum temperature at 14.6°C
byline: Nuwara Eliya recorded Sri Lanka’s lowest minimum temperature at 14.6°C on today (26), the Department of Meteorology’s daily temperature report said.

title: Bribery Commission urged to probe Chief Justice
byline: The National Trade Union and Civil Front has called on the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption to launch a comprehensive investigation into allegations made in Parliament concerning Chief Justice Priyathbandhu Surasena.

title: Legal action launched over illegal sand mining in Paranthan Proposed Reserve
byline: Forest conservation authorities have initiated legal action following complaints of illegal sand mining and soil transportation in the Paranthan Proposed Reserve in the Nedunkerny Divisional Secretariat Division of Vavuniya District.

title: Trump says all mines cleared from Strait of Hormuz
byline: US President Donald Trump has said that the US Navy has removed or detonated all mines in the Strait of Hormuz - the vital waterway which Iran has largely closed since the beginning of the war in the Middle East.

title: Dolly Parton dies
byline: World-renowned singer Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, foreign media reported.

title: Sea waves up to 3m possible along southern coast
byline: The Meteorological Department has warned of a possibility of sea wave heights of around 2.0 to 3.0 metres in the sea areas extending from Colombo to Pottuvil via Galle, Matara and Hambantota.

title: Union urges railways to withdraw legal action against SLRSMU Chief Secretary
byline: The Joint Development Officers’ Union has urged the General Manager of Sri Lanka Railways to immediately withdraw the decision to initiate legal action against the Chief Secretary of the Sri Lanka Railways Station Masters’ Union (SLRSMU) for publicly highlighting shortcomings in the administration of the Railway Department.

title: Jetstar launches direct Melbourne-Colombo flights
byline: Australian airline Jetstar has launched direct flights between Melbourne and Colombo, strengthening air connectivity between Sri Lanka and Australia.

title: Railway Unions raise concerns over lack of special trains during school holidays
byline: For the first time in history, no special trains have been scheduled during the current school holidays, while no discussions have been held on the work that needs to be carried out during the holiday period, the railway unions said.

title: Fire kills 14 newborns at major hospital in Pakistan, officials say
byline: A fire at a hospital’s maternity ward in a major government hospital in Pakistan’s capital killed at least 14 newborn babies early on Wednesday, according to hospital officials and the government.

title: Brazil fines TikTok owner ByteDance for unlawful processing of teenagers’ data
byline: Brazil’s data ‌protection authority, ANPD, has fined TikTok owner ByteDance 153.8 million reais ($29.81 million) for allegedly violating the country’s General Data Protection Law, according to a decision published in the official gazette on Tuesday.

title: Government not delaying Provincial Council Polls - Nalinda
byline: Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa yesterday said the Government’s position is to hold the Provincial Council elections at the earliest possible opportunity, once the necessary legislation is approved by Parliament.

title: Man declared dead in custody turns up alive at his own funeral house
byline: An unusual incident has been reported from Kohobankulama in Galgamuwa after a man who was officially reported dead while in prison unexpectedly returned home.

title: Sri Lanka’s 74 major reservoirs hold 35% of total capacity
byline: Water storage across country’s 74 major reservoirs has reached 1,182,385 acre-feet, equivalent to 35% of their combined gross capacity, according to the latest reservoir data.

title: Canada hits US with counter-tariffs on more than 700 products
byline: Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs against the United States as the trade war between Washington and Ottawa escalates, impacting hundreds of products.

title: Self-test for HIV, order condoms and lubricants online
byline: As health officials step up efforts to scale up HIV testing, people are encouraged to use the KNOW4SURE.LK online platform to access HIV prevention and testing services, including self-testing for HIV and discreetly ordering condoms and lubricants.

title: 133 Indians missing in Nepal flash flood; 95 killed; Bihar, UP borders on alert
byline: At least 133 Indians are among the over 400 persons missing with at least 95 deaths confirmed after massive flash floods swept through Nepal’s northern Rasuwa district near the Tibet border on Wednesday, washing away homes, vehicles, bridges and infrastructure project sites. The disaster has also triggered an alert in Bihar, which shares a border with Nepal, as floodwaters continue to move downstream.

title: Devastating flash flood on Nepal-Tibet border kills nine, hundreds of tourists missing
byline: A wall of mud and rock appeared to collapse ​into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China’s Tibet on Wednesday, triggering catastrophic flooding on the Nepali side that killed at least nine people and left ‌hundreds of tourists missing.

title: Yala National Park Blocks 1 and 2 to close temporarily
byline: The Wildlife Department has announced that Blocks 1 and 2 of Yala National Park will be temporarily closed to the public from September 14 to October 15.

title: Jerome Fernando’s Glorious Church becomes first Sri Lankan Church to register with UK Charity Commission
byline: Under the leadership of Jerome Fernando, his ‘The Glorious Church’ continues to expand and formalize its operations across its four branches in the United Kingdom, a statement from Jerome Fernando’s office said.

title: Sri Lanka stands in full solidarity with government, people of Nepal
byline: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said he is deeply saddened by the devastating floods reported in Rasuwa District and other parts of Nepal.
